result.summary:
The engine and protocol parts of Moshe's soft phase (D42) are built and tested. The leave-guard snapshot is now taken at the first loss event.

What a drop does now:
- A dropped connection gets a 10 s soft phase. The player is only marked; nothing freezes, nothing is released, and every timer keeps running.
- If he is not back by then, today's hard phase starts at softEndsAt: 15 s of grace, then a freeze (2 players) or a release (3–4 players). Abandonment is therefore 25 s after the drop.
- After any return he may send up to 8 moves made offline (`offlineMove`) within 5 s. Each is decided on the board as it is when it arrives. If the cell is taken, filled, the digit was tried, or all nine of it are placed, the move is refused with no trace and no penalty.

ENGINE (packages/engine)
- rules.ts: four new rules with defaults: softGraceMs 10000, offlineMovesMax 8, offlineMovesWindowMs 5000, interfereSoftOffline false. The header names D42. Older configs that lack them read as off, so old logs replay unchanged.
- types.ts:
  - PlayerState gets optional `softEndsAt?` and `offlineWindow?: {until, left}`.
  - The disconnect action gets `soft?`.
  - New PlayerAction `offlineMove {cell, digit, thinkMs}`, new RejectReason 'offlineClosed', and a new event `playerConnectionLost {playerId, softEndsAt}`.
  - placedCorrect and placedWrong get an optional `offline?: true`.
- engine.ts:
  - disconnect(soft) and a goHard() extracted from today's code.
  - A new 'softEnd' timer that also runs while the game is paused. DUE_ORDER is now interferenceEnd 0, grace 1, softEnd 2, lockExpire 3, turnExpire 4.
  - reconnect accepts a soft player. A soft player's own actions are refused 'disconnected'.
  - Interference at a soft target is refused 'targetDisconnected' unless the rule allows it. The 'turns' rotation skips soft players.
  - `place` now goes through placeDigit; the new helpers are digitTried and lockCell.
  - The `offlineMove` handler does every check before the first event. It locks the cell if needed (releasing his other lock as 'switch'), ignores his own re-lock wait, clamps thinkMs to [0, thinkTimeMs] (NaN counts as thinkTimeMs), and marks the move `offline: true`.
  - New export abandonmentAt(state, id).
- evolve.ts:
  - playerConnectionLost sets softEndsAt and takes the leave-guard snapshot with `??`, so the first loss wins and the hard phase keeps it.
  - playerDisconnected clears the soft fields.
  - playerReconnected deletes leaveStandings and softEndsAt, and opens the window only when softGraceMs > 0 and offlineMovesMax > 0.

  - Surrender, abandonment and gameOver clear both fields. A window whose time has passed is dropped at the next event.
  - New export isSoftOffline(p).

- The docs for GameHost, ClientMessage and PROTOCOL_VERSION are updated: the change is additive, and the version stays 1.

result.summary:
The server side of Moshe's soft phase (D42) is built and tested.

What the server does now:
- A connection that drops gets the soft phase first. That covers no goodbye, a dead socket, the heartbeat, the app going to the background, an abuse kick, and a reconnection whose socket died halfway.

  - The player is only marked (playerConnectionLost) and the game goes on. The engine's own softEnd timer starts today's 15 s grace at softEndsAt.
  - The seat is held until `abandonmentAt(state, id)` plus RECONNECT_SLACK_MS, so for the soft phase and the grace. Abandonment comes 25 s after the drop.
- A deliberate leave (CONSENTED) stays hard at once, and it also hardens a soft phase.
- launch(): a seat that dropped before the game (countdown, rated set-up) starts soft. A seat that left on purpose starts hard. holdSeatBeforeGame adds softGraceMs to the hold.
- `offlineMove` goes through the ordinary action path. A refused move goes to its sender only, as `rejected`, with no trace.
- The black-screen end-of-game seat handling is unchanged: holdSeatAfterGame, sawEnd and autoDispose.

- metrics.ts has a new ConnectionStats class, used once per server inside GameMetrics and once per room.
- GameMetricsReport gets `connections {soft, backInSoft, hard, backHard}` and `offlineMoves {applied, lost by reason}`.

findings.title: Polling stops after ~46.5 s and nothing re-reads when the 2-minute TTL runs out, so an unconfirmed rating can stay on Home indefinitely
findings.failure: The ruling in DECISIONS.md says to re-read /v1/me with backoff until the games count goes up and give up after 2 min. SPEC §4.3 and DECISIONS-PENDING 3.24 promise: "אם השרת לא שמר את המשחק תוך 2 דקות, מוצג הערך של השרת". In the code, the reads happen at 1.5, 4.5, 10.5, 22.5 and 46.5 s (the sum of confirmDelaysMs). After the last one, finish() refreshes progress once and stops. optimisticTtlMs (120 s) is only checked inside adopt(), so the optimistic entry goes away only when some later GET /v1/me is adopted. Scenario: the server's GameRecorder exhausts its retries and never stores the game, and the player stays on Home (no new focus, no foreground). Home keeps showing the rating the server never stored, past 2 minutes and with no end. A second case: the server stores the game later than 46.5 s, for example after a slow DB or a soft-grace abandonment whose leave was not delivered. Then the only progress refresh already ran before the store, so XP, level, league and games/win%/streak stay old until the player leaves Home and comes back.
findings.fix: Make the client act at the TTL. One option: when the attempts run out unconfirmed, schedule one more read (fetchMe, then refreshProgress) at optimisticTtlMs after the end. Pass the TTL into RankedRefreshDeps; do not hard-code it. The other option: keep the last raw server Me in authStore, and from showRankedResult set a timer at expiresAt that sets me again from withPendingRatings(lastServerMe, pendingRatings, now()). Either way, test it with ManualScheduler: no confirmation, then at 120 s Home shows the server's value.

findings.title: refreshMyProgress has no ordering guard, so an older progress answer can overwrite the one read after the store was confirmed
findings.failure: The fix works in two steps. Home's focus (and the foreground handler) call refreshMyProgress() at once, possibly before the server has stored the game. RankedRefresh calls refreshProgress() only after a GET /v1/me shows the game stored. refreshMyProgress, adoptProgress and adoptCard take whatever answer comes back last, with no request sequence (unlike fetchMe, which got a seq/meAdopted guard in this item). Scenario: the player taps "לבית" at T+1.4 s, and Home's progress GET goes out while the game is not yet stored. The server stores at T+1.45 s. RankedRefresh reads at T+1.5 s, sees the game stored, and its progress GET returns the new XP at T+1.9 s. Then Home's slower first GET (a slow mobile network) returns at T+2.3 s, and adoptProgress writes the old XP, level, league and games/win%/streak over the new ones. RankedRefresh has already finished, and Home is still in focus, so the card stays old until the next focus or foreground. That is the symptom Moshe reported, for the progress half of the card.
findings.fix: Add a request sequence to refreshMyProgress, the same way as in fetchMe: `const seq = ++progressRequests;` before the calls, and after the await `if (seq < progressAdopted) return; progressAdopted = seq;` before adoptProgress/adoptCard. Reset both counters when the owner changes (forgetProgress / onAuth). Add an appProgress test: two refreshMyProgress calls in flight, the first one resolving last, and the later answer must stay.

findings.title: The foreground re-take cannot restore keep-awake after the Android Activity is recreated, because the native manager skips addFlags while the tag is still held
findings.failure: In expo-keep-awake 57.0.2 on Android, ExpoKeepAwakeManager.activate(tag) calls addFlags(FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON) only `if (!isActivated)`, that is, only when the tag set is empty. The flag lives on the Activity's window. MainActivity's configChanges leave out fontScale and density. Concrete case: Moshe sends the app to the background and changes the system font size or display size, so Android recreates MainActivity with a new window that does not have the flag. RN then stops the old surface and mounts a new root. The old root's cleanup calls deactivateKeepAwake('sudoku-fight') while there is no current Activity (ReactHost.onHostDestroy cleared it). That call rejects before `tags.remove`, so 'sudoku-fight' stays in the set. The new root's activate, and the AppState 'active' re-take this hook adds, both hit `isActivated == true` and never add the flag to the new window. The screen then turns off on the phone's timeout for the rest of the run. That is exactly the failure Moshe reported. The comment's claim that the re-take on foreground recovers a failed activation holds only when the tag was never stored. Whether it happens depends on timing (the deactivate can also land after the new Activity resumes), but nothing in the code prevents it.
findings.fix: Re-apply the flag on every return to the foreground, not just re-add the tag. In the 'active' listener, release and take in sequence, for example `safely(() => keepAwake.deactivateKeepAwake(tag).catch(report).then(() => keepAwake.activateKeepAwakeAsync(tag)))`. When our tag is the only one, deactivate clears the flag on the current window and empties the set, and activate then adds the flag to the current window. The screen does not blink, because both calls run while the app is in the foreground. Add a keepAwake.test case with a fake module that copies the native short-circuit (it adds the 'flag' only when the set is empty), simulates a lost window, and asserts that the flag is back after appState.set('active').

findings.title: Screen reader announces a stale rating range after the 'nobody else' notice goes away
findings.failure: `rangeLine` is set once, the first time a range shows (`if (m.range && !m.alone && rangeLine === null)`), and never cleared. `line = m.alone ? aloneTitle : rangeLine`. Example: Ana starts while Ben is in reach, so the initial ±50 range '1150 עד 1250' is announced. Ben leaves, so Ana is alone and the notice is announced. At 30 s Cyd joins and `alone` turns false. `line` goes back to the old rangeLine, so the Announcer (re-announces whenever `line` changes) says 'מחפש יריב בטווח דירוג 1150 עד 1250'. The card on screen shows ±200 (1000–1400), so TalkBack/VoiceOver users hear the wrong numbers. The existing test covers only the alone-first order, where rangeLine is still null.
findings.fix: Reset the line while alone so it is rebuilt from the current range when someone turns up. For example, add `if (m.alone && rangeLine !== null) setRangeLine(null);` next to the existing adjust-in-render. Add a MatchScreen test for range → alone → someone (at a later elapsedMs) that expects the current range in announced().

findings.title: Timeout 'alone' text says nobody searched during the whole minute, but nextRange is only checked at the timeout moment
findings.failure: `timeout.nextRange` is `queue.nextRangeOf(ticket)`, checked only at the moment of the timeout. TimeoutView then shows 'עדיין אין שחקנים אחרים…' with timeout.aloneBody: 'חיפשנו דקה שלמה, ואף שחקן אחר לא חיפש משחק כזה' / 'We searched a whole minute and no one else looked for this game'. Example: Ben (250 away) searches from 10 s to 45 s, so Ana sees the range card with Ben in it. Ben then matches with Cyd, or cancels. At 60 s Ana gets nextRange null, and the screen says nobody looked for this game all minute, which contradicts what she just saw. The same happens on the extended search's second timeout.
findings.fix: Either track it on the server: add `Entry.sawOthers` (set in sendSearching when nextRange !== null, reset on a new search) and send the timeout as alone only when nextRange is null and sawOthers is false. Or reword timeout.aloneBody_* (he/en) to the present tense, e.g. 'חיפשנו {{time}}, וכרגע אין אף שחקן אחר שמחפש משחק כזה…'. Add a service.test case: a candidate joins and leaves mid-search, then the timeout.

result.reason:
The code does what the claim says, but this is the behaviour the approved design chose, not a defect. The scenario is also very narrow.

What the code does (confirmed): reads after a ranked game happen at 1.5, 4.5, 10.5, 22.5 and 46.5 s (confirmDelaysMs in apps/mobile/src/config/account.ts:49). After the last read, finish() refreshes progress once and stops (apps/mobile/src/progress/rankedRefresh.ts:117-119). The 120 s TTL is checked only in withPendingRatings, which adopt() calls (apps/mobile/src/api/me.ts:212, apps/mobile/src/auth/authStore.ts:147). So an expired optimistic entry is dropped only on the next GET /v1/me. That read comes from Home focus or the app returning to the foreground (refreshMeIfStale, 30 s throttle: HomeScreen.tsx:98, appProgress.ts:196), or from the results screen's leave.

Why it is not a defect:
1. The ruling for this item (DECISIONS.md, rating-refresh) is "As designed". The design file docs/handoff/2026-10-15/designs/rating-refresh.json fixes this exact schedule: confirmDelaysMs [1500,3000,6000,12000,24000]. It defines optimisticTtlMs as "how long the game's own rating change is shown over older server answers; after that, the server's answer wins". So it is a guard on what an answer may override, not a timer.
2. The same design lists this exact case as an accepted risk: "Optimistic display: for up to optimisticTtlMs the phone may show a rating the server has not stored (if the write failed for good). It self-corrects on the next read after the TTL." Its risk list also says late or unpolled stores "rely on the throttled Home focus and foreground reads". The ruling's "(give up after 2 min)" summarises that TTL. It does not order polling to continue for 2 minutes.
3. The existing authStore test ("a game the server never stores: after optimisticTtlMs the server's answer wins") encodes the same lazy meaning: the correction happens on the next read.

How narrow the scenario is:
- Case 1 needs two things together. First, the server's GameRecorder must fail for good: all 5 tries fail (waits of 500 ms doubling, about 7.5 s in all), which means the database is down. Second, the player must then sit on Home for more than 2 minutes without navigating anywhere or sending the app to the background. Any focus or foreground event corrects it.
- Case 2 (stored after 46.5 s) needs a pathologically slow database. A left 2-player game has no optimistic value at all (change is null). Its reads start at graceMs 15 s + 2 s and go on to about 63.5 s, which covers an abandonment at about 25-30 s.

Neither case is what Moshe reported. He said the rating did not update until a restart, and the polling and optimistic display fix that.

The claim holds up against the code. In apps/mobile/src/progress/appProgress.ts:141-158, refreshMyProgress takes no request sequence. It sets status 'loading', awaits Promise.all(myProgress, player card), checks only that the owner is the same, and then calls adoptProgress/adoptCard without conditions. progressStore.ts:74-81 also writes whatever comes in, with no updatedAt comparison and no in-flight dedupe. So when two calls overlap, the one that resolves last wins.

Both callers are wired to run in exactly the post-game window:
- HomeScreen.tsx:93-101 calls refreshMyProgress() on every focus, so the moment the player taps "to home".
- The AppState 'active' handler in appProgress.ts:191-197 does the same.
- RankedRefresh calls it through rankedRefresh() (appProgress.ts:111) only after a GET /v1/me shows the game stored (rankedRefresh.ts:113-115, finish -> progress).

The server stores the result in the background, 1-3 s after the end and with retries (rating-refresh.json cause #2: GameRecorder writes games+1, XP and histories in one end transaction). confirmDelaysMs[0] is 1500 ms and waitMs is 0 for a normal end. So a Home GET that the server answered before the store, and a RankedRefresh GET issued shortly after the store, can be in flight together.

Home's call also waits on Promise.all with the card GET. One slow leg is enough for its old progress to be adopted after RankedRefresh's new one. That can be a new TCP/TLS connection while Home fires refreshHome, refreshMeIfStale and 2 progress GETs at once, or a slow mobile link.

Nothing corrects it afterwards. RankedRefresh does exactly one progress read after confirmation and then stops (wait=null). Home's useFocusEffect does not fire again while Home stays in focus. The foreground handler needs an app state change. So the old XP, level, league and games/win%/streak stay on the card, which is Moshe's symptom ("doesn't update automatically; after reopening it did"). This matches the ruling in DECISIONS.md, which says to refresh progress/card after the server confirms. The same item added a seq/meAdopted guard to fetchMe (authStore.ts:85-96, 428-435) for out-of-order answers, and its design lists that test (rating-refresh.json test line 159). The progress half of the same flow got no such guard, which is an inconsistent gap.

Caveat: the window is timing-dependent and narrow. The old answer has to arrive more than about one round trip after a request that was sent after the store. So this is a real but low-probability race, not the main cause of the reported symptom. The proposed fix (a seq counter in refreshMyProgress, reset in forgetProgress/on owner change, plus a two-in-flight test) is appropriate.

I tried to refute this and couldn't. The scenario can happen, and the behaviour is wrong.

1. `SearchView` keeps its state between server messages. `MatchScreen.tsx:145` renders `<SearchView key="search" .../>` with a fixed key, so `rangeLine` survives every `searching` message while the screen stays in 'search'.

2. The range line is built once and never rebuilt. `SearchView.tsx:61` sets `rangeLine` only when `m.range && !m.alone && rangeLine === null`. Nothing ever sets it back to null.

3. Line 69 is `line = m.alone ? aloneTitle : rangeLine`. The `Announcer` (`game/connection/Announcer.tsx`) speaks whenever `line` changes:
   - iOS: through a `useEffect` on `[line]`.
   - Android: through a live region on the text.

4. The server really sends this order. Per `service.ts:46-49` and `:379-381`, it sends a new `searching` whenever `queue.nextRange(userId)` changes. That value changes whenever someone Ana could meet joins or leaves (`matcher.ts` `nextRanges`, rule 7). The client copies each `nextRange` (`net/matchmaking.ts:519`), and `matchModel.ts:176` sets `alone = nextRange === null`.

So the order range → alone → someone is easy to reach:
- Ben is in reach (inside the maximum range) but outside Ana's starting ±50, so Ana's `nextRange` is not null and the starting range is spoken.
- Ben cancels, so `nextRange` becomes null, `alone` turns true and the notice is spoken.
- Cyd joins later, so `nextRange` is not null again and `alone` turns false.

At that point `line` goes back to the old `rangeLine`, and screen-reader users hear the starting numbers. The card shows the current, wider `m.range`.

This is not intended behaviour:
- The existing test `MatchScreen.test.tsx:285` ("someone turns up: the notice goes and the range is back (and said)") expects the current range to be spoken: 1162–1412 at 15 s.
- That test only covers the order where the notice comes first, while `rangeLine` is still null. That is why it passes.
- The comment at line 68 says the range comes back "again only if it ends and comes back". Saying numbers that differ from what the card shows breaks that intent and gives screen-reader users wrong information.

The ruling and Moshe's words don't excuse it. The matchmaking ruling ("nextRange … null → no other players are searching") requires the range to return when someone appears, so the spoken range should be the current one.

The proposed fix is sound: reset `rangeLine` while `alone`, so it is rebuilt from the current range when someone turns up. A test for range → alone → someone at a later elapsedMs is also needed.

The scenario can happen, but the code does what the approved design says, so this is not an implementation defect.

How the scenario happens: in apps/server/src/matchmaking/service.ts:458, timedOut() sends `nextRange: queue.nextRangeOf(ticket)`. matcher.ts:424 computes this from the tickets still in the queue at that moment only. matchModel.ts:187 sets alone = timeout.nextRange === null. TimeoutView.tsx:51-56 then shows timeout.aloneTitle/aloneBody. In he/match.json:91 the body reads 'חיפשנו {{time}}, ואף שחקן אחר לא חיפש משחק כזה'. So if a compatible player is in the queue mid-search and then cancels or is matched elsewhere, the past-tense body is wrong. This also happens on the second timeout after "keep searching", because searchStart is kept and the body says "2 דקות".

Why the behaviour is still not wrong given Moshe's words and the rulings:
1. DECISIONS.md, matchmaking: "Recommended defaults as in the design … 60 s timeout stays with its own wording for the alone case". The design (designs/matchmaking.json) says the timeout's nextRange "is computed at the timeout instant" (design §1c / §3d). §10 of the design gives these exact aloneTitle/aloneBody strings, and its test list pins the body 'חיפשנו דקה שלמה, ואף שחקן אחר לא חיפש משחק כזה…'. The code matches the design word for word.
2. Moshe's words ("אם לא יהיה טווח הבא זה אומר שאין") define null as "there are none now", and the server sends exactly that.
3. The design already uses the "no one else" wording loosely on purpose. A blocked player (the block must not be revealed), or one beyond ±300, can search the whole minute and still give null and the same "אף שחקן אחר לא חיפש" text (design §11 edge cases). Being imprecise about timing fits that accepted looseness. It is not a deviation from the design.
4. The claim says Ana "sees the range card with Ben in it", and SearchView.tsx:106-121 shows otherwise. The range card shows only her own widening range. No other player is ever shown, and the design's decision "no next-range marker" confirms this. So nothing she was shown contradicts the timeout text in any explicit way.
5. The proposed server fix (sawOthers) would make alone=false while nextRange is null. That would require a non-null nextRange when nobody is there, or new semantics, which breaks the protocol meaning the design set. The alternative is rewording to the present tense. That changes copy Moshe approved through the ruling, so it would be a suggestion for Moshe, not a bug fix.

At most this is an optional copy refinement to offer Moshe (for example, a present-tense aloneBody). It is not a defect against his request or the rulings.

(2) The set outlives the Activity. ReactHost is held by MainApplication, and KeepAwakeModule/manager is per React instance.

(3) The AndroidManifest MainActivity configChanges leave out fontScale and density, so a font-size or display-size change recreates the Activity. The new window does not have the flag.

**Can it happen?**
- Attempt 1 of a reconnect has no delay (`comeBack()`; the 250 ms is the wait before attempt 2).
- Colyseus 0.18's `checkReconnectionToken` forcibly closes the old connection when a reconnect arrives with its token. So a token reconnect does not wait for the server's heartbeat to notice the drop, and a full cycle under 1 s is possible. Ways to get there:
  - The OS closes the socket on a network switch (`onLeave`), followed by an immediate reconnect.
  - A quick background and foreground.
- The condition: N moves sent in the first flush, M of them sent again, and the second flush arriving less than (N+M-8)×125 ms after the first. Examples:
  - 8 sent, 3 refused: under 375 ms.
  - 8 sent, all 8 refused: under 1 s.

So it is reachable, but it is a narrow race:
- It needs 5 or more moves made offline (8 at most).
- The second drop must land in the single round-trip after the server got the moves but before the phone got the answers.
- The reconnect must finish fast.

The claim's "250 ms" detail is slightly off, but that only makes the race easier.

**Is the behaviour wrong?** Yes. The 'grace' ruling in `DECISIONS.md` says an offline move is lost only when the cell isn't free for him on return, with no penalty and a short message. Here the move is never judged and no message comes.

**Where the claim overstates:**
- "For the rest of the game" is too strong. Once someone fills the cell, filled takes precedence and the queued digit disappears from the board.
- Even so, the entry stays in the queue:
  - It still counts toward `offlineMovesMax` on the next loss.
  - At the next drop it is sent again, and the "did not count" message comes long after the move was made.

Real, but rare.

result.item: Fix 12 CONFIRMED defects (keep-awake, grace x5, black-screen, rating-refresh, penalty x2, matchmaking, givens)
result.summary:
All 12 defects are fixed at the root, and each has a test that reproduces it. `npm run verify` is green: lint, `tsc -b` and i18n (0 errors) pass, and Jest passes 372 suites with 8644 tests. Prettier is clean on every changed file. No new UI strings.

1. **Keep-awake** (`services/keepAwake.ts`): every take now releases the tag first, then takes it. This happens on mount and on every return to the foreground. The take is skipped if the hook has let go in the meantime. The test uses a fake module that copies Android's ExpoKeepAwakeManager: the flag is set only when the tag set is empty, and calls fail when there is no Activity. It covers a recreated window, a tag left by a failed release, a fast unmount, and start-up failures.

2. **Offline moves when both players dropped**:
   - Engine (`evolve.ts`): an offline window does not expire while the game is frozen. On `gameResumed`, a window opened during the freeze runs a full `offlineMovesWindowMs` from the resume. A window opened before the freeze keeps the time it had left.
   - Phone (`remoteGameHost.ts`): `flushOffline` holds the queue, the held cell and the releases while the game is paused. It sends them all when the next event shows the game is no longer paused (`flushOnResume`). A new disconnect clears the hold.
   - Tests: two engine tests and a remoteGameHost test (both offline, I return first, the moves wait and then count).

3. **`selfOffline` without offline play**:
   - `ConnectionStatus` now carries `playable`, mapped from `offlinePlay.playable`.
   - `connectionModel` returns `selfOffline` only when the phone can play on. In a game already frozen for the opponent, the freeze screen stays. In any other case it shows Self-Reconnecting at once.
   - In GameScreen, `withoutServer()` turns off `canSurrender` and `reactionReady` on my card while `online.status === 'reconnecting'`.
   - Tests in connectionModel and connectionStatus, plus a GameScreenOnline test (frozen game, then my connection drops: the freeze stays and Surrender is disabled).

4. **"The opponent left" seconds**: RemoteGameHost tracks how each other player's absence began (`absences`; `playerConnectionLost` means a drop, a bare `playerDisconnected` means a hard leave) and exposes it as `OnlineInfo.hardLeavers`. `opponentLeftOf` uses `graceMs` alone for a hard leaver, and the soft phase plus the grace otherwise. Tests in connectionModel and remoteGameHost.

5. **Rate-limited `offlineMove`**:
   - Each queue entry now keeps `sentAt`. A sent move with no answer after `offlineAnswerTimeoutMs` (3000) is sent again (`watchOfflineAnswers`, `resetSentBy`).
   - A refusal of an `offlineMove` whose queue entry is already gone (an old copy) is silent, so there is no false 'lost' toast.
   - The server gate's `offlineMove` limit went from 8 to 16 per second (two bursts).
   - Tests in offlinePlay, remoteGameHost and gate.

6. **Lock cancelled offline**: `OfflinePlayBook` records the cells let go of offline (cancel, or a switch to another cell). `end()` now returns a `ReturnPlan {held, letGo}`. On return, if the server still shows my lock on one of those cells, and it is not the held cell or a queued one, the phone sends `release` before the moves. Two remoteGameHost tests: cancel offline, and a switch to a cell that was taken meanwhile.

7. **Native window during the end hold** (GameScreen):
   - `showResults` checks for open windows again inside `open()`. If one is up, it closes it, waits for it to leave, and has its own ceiling (`go`).
   - When the game is over, the card menu, the picker and the arsenal close. CardMenu gets no moderation items. `openReport` and `openBlock` are guarded by `ended.current`.
   - GameScreenOnline test: the menu is open when the opponent surrenders.

8. **Older progress answer overwriting a newer one** (`appProgress.ts`): reads are numbered (`progressReads` / `progressTaken`), and an answer older than one already taken is dropped. When the account changes, reads still in flight are dropped too. Test: two reads in flight, the older one answers last.

9. **Pips too wide**: new `pipsForWidth()` in `cardModel` with `metrics.compact.twoPipsMinWidth = 110`. A 3-player card shows two pips; a 4-player card, or any card with ×n, shows the last one only. The pips also shrink and clip from the start (oldest first), and the score row is capped at the card width. Tests in cardModel and PlayerCard.

10. **Spec §6.5 example**: rewritten without D5, using X = 7, Y = 6 → ‎−3.5, with the LRM kept.

11. **Stale range announcement** (`SearchView`): the spoken range line is reset while nobody else is searching. MatchScreen test: range → alone → someone at 15 s announces the current range.

12. **Loading tip**: `TOP_MOVE_POINTS` is now per game type (fast 6.5, normal 9.5, hard 12), and ConnectingView passes `match.gameType`. The test now measures the best opening move per game type over `packages/engine/data/puzzles.json` (both pools) instead of the CSV.

deviations: Item 4: I track how the absence began on the phone, in RemoteGameHost (exposed as OnlineInfo.hardLeavers), not in engine state. The snapshot-size budget is about 100 B. Fallback: an opponent first seen already hard in a snapshot counts as a drop (soft + grace = 25 s), as before.

Item 5: I did not add a new 'rejected' reason for rate-limited messages. Instead the server limit is 16/s (two bursts) and the phone resends a move with no answer after offlineAnswerTimeoutMs = 3000. A late refusal of an old copy is now silent (no false 'lost' toast). One more consequence: an offlineMove refused after the end cleared the queue no longer shows a toast either.

Item 6: the release is sent only for cells the player let go of offline (cancel, or a switch to another cell), not for every server lock that is neither held nor queued. A lock that only ran out with the soft phase is still kept through a hard-phase freeze, as before.

Item 7: the extra check inside open() covers any remaining race. The main protection is that, once the game is over, the card menu closes and loses its report/block items. The new test therefore checks that no window can open during the hold. The late-wait branch itself is not exercised by a test, because there is no longer a way to open a window during the hold.
Item 2: a window opened before the freeze also stands still during it (it keeps its remaining time from the resume). The proposal only covered windows opened during the freeze.
openIssues: The gate limit change (offlineMove 16/s) and the engine change (offline window stands still during a freeze) need a server deploy. With an old server, a frozen return's held-back moves can get 'offlineClosed' if the other player returns more than 5 s later. ENGINE_VERSION was not bumped, per DECISIONS.md (integration step).

Device-only checks: STAGE7 new check 2ג (cancel while offline; both phones offline, the first back waits for the freeze to end); QA row 8 keep-awake after a font/display-size change in the background (release build only); QA row 13 pip widths at a large system font.

Cases where the new ReturnPlan.letGo is not released: if the game freezes at the return and the connection drops again before it resumes, the held-back plan (held cell and let-go releases) is dropped. The next loss restarts letGo, so the server's kept lock may come back to the player. This is an edge case and I accepted it.
notesForOtherItems: OfflinePlayBook API changed: end(now) returns ReturnPlan {held, letGo} (was CellIndex|null). markSent(entry, clientSeq, at) has a new phone-time argument. QueuedEntry has a new sentAt. There are new oldestSentAt / resetSentBy(at).
RemoteHostOptions.offlineAnswerTimeoutMs (default 3000) is new. OnlineInfo.hardLeavers?: readonly PlayerId[] is new (optional, so hand-built OnlineInfo literals still compile).

ConnectionStatus reconnecting/resyncing have an optional playable (connectionStatusOf fills it from offlinePlay.playable; absent means true). ConnectionModelOptions.hardLeavers is new. Exact-object tests of reconnecting statuses must include playable.
TOP_MOVE_POINTS is now Record<GameType, number>, not a number. The new pipsForWidth(pips, width) is in components/player/cardModel; a 4-player compact card shows one pip.

GameScreen: new `over` adjust-in-render that closes the arsenal, picker and card menu when the game ends. CardMenu moderation is null once the game is over. The new withoutServer() turns off canSurrender/reactionReady while online.status === 'reconnecting'. The interference item touches the same file (⚡ slot, card menu): keep these.

evolve.ts: offline-window expiry is skipped while the pre-event status is 'paused', and gameResumed re-times every offlineWindow. A replay of a game played before this change that had a pause together with an offline window can differ; this relies on the planned ENGINE_VERSION bump.
